land.text: the Western Khanate in Transoxiana, 'making Samarkand the capital'

predecessors.note: 'The Khanate split into the Eastern and Western Khanates in the 1040s' (the page gives no year); Cliopatria's two rows begin in 1046, which is used here. The unified Khanate is the dossier kara-khanids (840-1045).

land.text: Samarkand and Transoxiana: Muhammad II 'executed Uthman ... and finally extinguished the Western Karakhanid state' in 1212

successors.note: Bukhara had passed to Khwarazm in 1207 and Samarkand was taken in 1210; the Fergana valley and Tashkent oasis had gone to the Qara Khitai in 1137 (see kara-khitans).

capitals.name: Samarkand
capitals.note: Infobox 'Samarkand (1040-1212)'; the Western Khanate's capital throughout ('making Samarkand the capital'). Coordinates from the gazetteer.

rulers.name: Ibrahim Tamghach Khan
rulers.note: 'c. 1040-1068' in the page's ruler list (the extracted table was flagged as garbled); the page: 'considered by Muslim historians as a great ruler'; he founded the first madrasa in Samarkand.

rulers.name: Shams al-Mulk Nasr
rulers.note: Shams al-Mulk page: 'a Karakhanid ruler in Transoxiana from 1068 to 1080'; died 1080 and 'succeeded by his brother Khizr Khan'.

rulers.note: Reign years from the Kara-Khanid page's ruler list.

rulers.name: Ahmad
rulers.note: Ruler list 1081-1089. The Malik-Shah I page has 'the Western Kara-Khanid ruler Ahmed' captured by the Seljuks after the fall of Samarkand in 1087, and the Kara-Khanid page has the ulama securing Ahmad's execution in 1095; the dates do not agree.

rulers.name: Muhammad Arslan Khan
rulers.note: Ruler list 1102-1129 (the page names the Kalyan minaret at Bukhara as his). Gaps 1097-1102 and 1129-1141 are in the list; the Qatwan page names his son Mahmud II as the ruler who 'sought protection from his Seljuk overlord, Sanjar' after 1137, without reign years.

rulers.name: Ibrahim Tabghach Khan
rulers.note: Ruler list 1141-1156; the Qara Khitai page: in early 1156 'the Karluks killed Ibrahim Tabghach Khan, the Western Karakhanid ruler of Samarkand'. The Qatwan page: Yelü Dashi 'appointed Mahmud's brother Ibrahim as ruler of Samarkand' in 1141.

rulers.name: Ibrahim Arslan Khan
rulers.note: Ruler list 1178-1202; the years 1156-1178 are missing from the list.

rulers.name: Uthman ibn Ibrahim
rulers.note: Ruler list 1202-1212; executed by Muhammad II of Khwarazm in 1212.

keyframe_review.note: 1046-1055, 326,270 km2 (Transoxiana from Bukhara and Samarkand to Khujand and Chach, Termez on the Oxus). The page puts the Western Khanate in Transoxiana with Samarkand as capital and the Oxus as the frontier with the Ghaznavids ('The Oxus River thus became the boundary'); it gives no area, so the infobox comparison is not possible. The shape differs from 1056 by 30 cells on the south-east edge (Pamir foothills), which no page dates: unverified.
1056-1065, 318,885 km2: the 1046 shape without 30 cells at 70.5-73.1 E, 37.6-40.3 N and with 2 cells added; unverified: page silent on this step.

1066-1071, 382,959 km2: the Fergana valley (218 cells, 55,000 km2, 70.0-73.8 E, 38.6-42.6 N) passes from Cliopatria's Eastern row to this one. Unverified and in tension with the pages: the Kara-Khanid page says 'When the two states were formed, Fergana fell into realm of the Eastern Khanate' and that 'The Fergana-Zhetysu areas became the border between the two states and were frequently contested'; the Malik-Shah I page has the Eastern ruler at Uzkand (Uzgen) in 1087; the Yelü Dashi page has him defeating the Western Karakhanids at Khujand in May 1137 and then consolidating power in the Ferghana valley and Tashkent. Kept as drawn; the ledger records the step at confidence 1.

Cliopatria's Great Seljuk Empire row (1085-1146) holds the same 1,279 cells; the pages instead keep the khanate alive under Seljuk overlordship ('For half a century, the Western Karakhanid Khanate was a vassal of the Seljuks'; the Seljuks 'largely controlled who was appointed ruler'). The Seljuk campaign is dated 1087 by the Malik-Shah I page and 1089 by the Kara-Khanid page; the Seljuk dossier should carry the vassal_start (counterpart western-karakhanid-khanate). Status change only: shape unchanged from the adjusted 1072 shape.

Yelü Dashi: 'In May 1137 he defeated a Western Karakhanid ruler at Khujand' and 'consolidated power in the Ferghana valley and Tashkent for several years'. From September 1141 (Qatwan) the khanate is a Qara Khitai vassal ('Despite losing to the Qara Khitai, the Karakhanid dynasty remained in power as their vassals'); the shape stays the same for the whole span.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1207-1212: Bukhara has passed to Khwarazm. Qara Khitai page's chronology for 1207: Muhammad II enters Bukhara; Kara-Khanid page: the Bukhara revolt of 1207 was 'used as a pretext to conquer Bukhara'. Samarkand falls to the Khwarezm-Shah in 1210 with Uthman as his ally and is held jointly until the 1212 revolt (contest in the ledger).

region.text: the Western Khanate in Transoxiana, 'making Samarkand the capital'

ledger.note: 1046: the Western Khanate of the Kara-Khanids is formed at Samarkand. 'The Khanate split into the Eastern and Western Khanates in the 1040s.' The page gives the decade, not the year; 1046 is Cliopatria's first year for the two rows.

1066: the Fergana valley passes from the Eastern to the Western Khanate. Cliopatria's step; the Kara-Khanid page is silent on the date ('Fergana fell into realm of the Eastern Khanate' when the two states were formed, 'frequently contested' afterwards). The page goes on: Fergana 'was later captured by Ibrahim and became part of the Western Khanate' (Ibrahim Tamghach Khan, khan to 1068), so the transfer is on the page and falls before 1068; only the year 1066 is Cliopatria's (reviewer ia-01-g).

region.text: Termez on the Oxus, taken by Malik-Shah in 1073

ledger.note: 1073: Malik-Shah drives the Kara-Khanids back and takes Termez. 'Malik-Shah went on a campaign to Transoxiana with his army in 1073' and 'headed towards Termez and captured Termez'; the page names the city, the Karakhanid ownership is the reading.

region.text: Bukhara and Samarkand, the Western Karakhanid country under a Seljuk governor

ledger.note: 1087: Malik-Shah invades Transoxiana. 'In 1087 ... Malik-Shah decided to organize another expedition to Transoxiana', took Kara-Khanid castles 'especially Bukhara, Samarkand, Balasagun, Isfijab and Kashgar', and 'the Western Kara-Khanid ruler Ahmed was captured by the Seljuks after the capture of Samarkand'. The Kara-Khanid page dates the Seljuk entry into Samarkand to 1089.

1089: Seljuk rule is established over Transoxiana and the khans become vassals. 'the entire Turkistan Region, up to the borders of China, was brought under Seljuk rule in 1089'; the Kara-Khanid infobox has 'Seljuk vassal (1089-1141)'. The Seljuk dossier should carry the matching vassal_start for this counterpart.

1137: Yelü Dashi defeats the Western Karakhanids at Khujand and takes the Fergana valley and Tashkent. 'In May 1137 he defeated a Western Karakhanid ruler at Khujand'; 'He consolidated power in the Ferghana valley and Tashkent for several years'. The Qara Khitai page: 'In 1137, he defeated the Western Karakhanids near Khujand'. The page gives the battle and the land, not the exact transfer of Fergana and Tashkent.

region.text: Bukhara, entered by Muhammad II in 1207

ledger.note: 1207: the Khwarezm-Shah takes Bukhara. The Qara Khitai page's chronology for 1207: Muhammad II enters Bukhara; the Kara-Khanid page: 'In 1207, the citizens of Bukhara revolted against the sadrs', which Muhammad 'used as a pretext to conquer Bukhara'. Neither page says Bukhara was then directly Western Karakhanid: the Qatwan page has Dashi let 'the Burhan family keep ruling Bukhara' in 1141, and the revolt of 1207 was against 'the sadrs', the religious leaders.

1210: the Khwarezm-Shah takes Samarkand after the Qara Khitai withdraw, allied to Uthman. 'In 1210, the Khwarezm-Shah took Samarkand after the Qara Khitai retreated'; Muhammad 'formed an alliance with the Western Karakhanid ruler Uthman ibn Ibrahim'. Until the revolt of 1212 the city is held by both.

1212: Samarkand revolts against the Khwarezmians; Muhammad retakes it. 'In 1212, the population of Samarkand staged a revolt against the Khwarezmians'; 'The Khwarezm-Shah returned, recaptured Samarkand and executed Uthman.'

region.text: Samarkand and the rest of Transoxiana

ledger.note: 1212: the Western Karakhanid state is extinguished. Muhammad 'demanded the submission of all leading Karakhanids, and finally extinguished the Western Karakhanid state'; 'the Western Khanate was extinguished by the Khwarazmian Empire in 1212'.

wars.name: Seljuk campaigns in Transoxiana

zones.text: Termez on the Oxus, taken by Malik-Shah in 1073

wars.outcome: Seljuk victory: Termez taken in 1073; Samarkand and Bukhara taken in 1087; 'the entire Turkistan Region, up to the borders of China, was brought under Seljuk rule in 1089', the khans kept as vassals.
wars.note: Alp Arslan was wounded in the 1072 campaign 'against the Karakhanids' and died days later; Malik-Shah's 1073 campaign followed a Kara-Khanid raid on Tukharistan in which his brother Ayaz was killed. The Kara-Khanid page dates the Seljuk entry into Samarkand to 1089.

wars.name: Qara Khitai conquest of the Fergana valley (Khujand)
wars.outcome: Qara Khitai victory near Khujand in May 1137; the Fergana valley and Tashkent oasis pass to the Qara Khitai.

wars.name: Battle of Qatwan
wars.outcome: Qara Khitai victory on 9 September 1141 on the Qatwan steppe north of Samarkand; Samarkand's khanate and Khwarazm become Qara Khitai vassals, Yelü Dashi appointing Mahmud's brother Ibrahim at Samarkand.
wars.note: No land changed hands: the Western Karakhanid shape is the same before and after; only the suzerain changes from the Seljuks to the Qara Khitai.

wars.name: Khwarazmian conquest of Transoxiana
wars.outcome: Bukhara taken in 1207, Samarkand in 1210; the revolt of Samarkand in 1212 ends in Uthman's execution and the end of the Western Karakhanid state.
wars.note: Uthman ibn Ibrahim allied with Muhammad against the Qara Khitai in 1210 and was killed by him in 1212.

certainty.note: Oasis and steppe frontiers throughout, no survey or treaty line; the Oxus was the line with the Ghaznavids and then the Seljuks ('The Oxus River thus became the boundary'), the Fergana-Zhetysu border with the Eastern Khanate was 'frequently contested'.

notes:
One state or three: Wikidata Q494354 is shared by Cliopatria's Kara-Khanids (850-1045), Eastern Kara-Khanids (1046-1138) and Western Karakhanid Khanate (1046-1084). The Kara-Khanid page lists one khanate that 'split into the Eastern and Western Khanates in the 1040s'; after the split the two are different states with different capitals (Samarkand against Balasagun and later Kashgar), and the dossier kara-khanids (840-1045) already hands the land to both. This dossier is the Western Khanate alone.
Start and end moved: Cliopatria's row runs 1046-1084 (the Seljuk takeover of Transoxiana); the pages keep the khanate alive to 1212 as a vassal of the Seljuks (1089-1141) and the Qara Khitai (1141-1212) and end it in 1212, so new keyframes _1085, _1137 and _1207 carry the shape to 1212. Cliopatria draws the same land as Great Seljuk Empire 1085-1146 and as Kara-Khitans from 1147 to 1209; the great-seljuk-empire dossier should carry vassal_start (1089) and vassal_end (1141) with counterpart western-karakhanid-khanate, and kara-khitans carries the vassal_start of 1141 and vassal_end of 1210. Where the layers are drawn is a decision for the compile stage.
Unsettled: (1) the Seljuk dates, 1087 (Malik-Shah I page) against 1089 (Kara-Khanid page; Cliopatria's Seljuk row starts in 1085); (2) the Fergana valley, which Cliopatria gives to the West in 1066 while the pages say the East held it at the split and the Qara Khitai took it from the West in 1137 (undated step, confidence 1); (3) the ruler list is from a garbled table and its dates conflict with the Malik-Shah I page (Ahmed captured 1087, executed 1095 against Ahmad 1081-1089); (4) Bukhara in 1207 is the Burhan sadrs' city, not clearly the khanate's. No page gives an area, so the infobox comparison was impossible. Pages: Kara-Khanid Khanate (three queries), Malik-Shah I, Shams al-Mulk Nasr (thin), Battle of Qatwan, Qara Khitai, Yelü Dashi: six distinct pages against a budget of 5.
Missing: the Ghaznavid frontier events of 1046-1065 and the Western Khanate's 12th-century wars with the Eastern Khanate (the Kara-Khanid page gives no dates), the Karluks who killed Ibrahim Tabghach Khan in 1156.
